text:
ashley (Support): Customer report: Android app drops mid-stream when they toggle airplane mode -> re-enables WiFi. After reconnect, the client receives a duplicate partial chunk and the customer was billed twice for the same generation. Repro steps + attached logs below.

mike (Android Eng): oh no. do we have client logs + server request ids?

ashley (Support): pasted client log snippet:
```
2026-03-15 14:12:01.223 INFO SSEClient Connecting to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
2026-03-15 14:12:05.341 WARN Network connection lost: AIRPLANE_MODE_TOGGLE
2026-03-15 14:12:05.342 ERROR Socket closed: ECONNRESET
2026-03-15 14:12:10.012 INFO Reconnecting...
2026-03-15 14:12:10.230 INFO SSEClient reconnected, resuming stream, lastEventId=evt-18723
2026-03-15 14:12:10.235 INFO Received chunk: {"delta":"Hello wor"}
2026-03-15 14:12:10.236 INFO Received chunk: {"delta":"ld\n"}
2026-03-15 14:12:10.237 INFO Received chunk (duplicate): {"delta":"Hello wor"}
```
Customer says the UI concatenated chunks and ended with duplicated prefix, and the billing dashboard shows 2x token counts for that call id (request_id: r-0a9c3).

samir (eng-sre): can you share the server-side request id/time from our logs? also which SDK version?

ashley (Support): server log snippet (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:05Z] INFO request_start request_id=r-0a9c3 client_ip=203.0.113.45 model=gpt-neo-compat
[2026-03-15T14:12:05Z] ERROR connection_lost socket_close reason=client_disconnect event_id=evt-18723 stream_state=partial_kv_cache
[2026-03-15T14:12:10Z] INFO request_resume request_id=r-0a9c3 resume_from_event=evt-18723 new_connection_id=conn-77a
[2026-03-15T14:12:12Z] INFO token_bill request_id=r-0a9c3 billed_tokens=82 note="billing increment after resume"
[2026-03-15T14:12:12Z] INFO token_bill request_id=r-0a9c3 billed_tokens=82 note="duplicate billing entry detected"
```

jordan (Support Lead): flagged as SEV-3 for now. Customer is asking for explanation + refund of duplicate charge. Please confirm whether resume path can duplicate output/charge.

samir (eng-sre): preliminary theory: when the client reconnects with lastEventId, our runtime attempted to continue from the KV cache but also retried the token generation path, producing overlapping deltas. Two billing events indicate both the original continuation and a resumed rerun were billed. We need to check retry/fallback logic in the resume handler — we should NOT re-run tokens for already-emitted sequence numbers.

mike (Android Eng): client is using our android-sdk v0.9.2. The SDK reconnect flow does: if socket closes unexpectedly -> backoff -> open new SSE with header `Last-Event-ID: <lastEventId>`. We rely on server to dedupe. Any known server-side idempotency header?

anna (Product): customer-facing ask: if this is possible, we should ship a mitigation we can enable per-tenant (extra-safe resume mode that returns 409 if resuming would re-run tokens) and proactively credit affected customers.

samir (eng-sre): immediate mitigation options:
- roll forward a hotfix to make resume handler verify `lastEventId` against a persisted sequence and return a special resume-ack that includes `resume_point` so client can discard already-received chunks.
- implement a short-lived server-side idempotency marker for in-flight request ids: if a reconnect arrives within Xs with same request_id and same resume point, return 200 with no extra billing.

mike (Android Eng): for a quick client-side workaround we can: detect duplicate repeating deltas by sequence or checksum and drop duplicates before rendering. But that doesn't solve billing/metrics. We'll push a small SDK patch to v0.9.3 to ignore repeated delta bodies when their `event.id` equals a previously-seen id.

ashley (Support): customer also shared a packet capture showing the reconnect sequence. here's a condensed extract:
```
-- before toggle --
: event: message
: id: evt-18723
: data: {"delta":"Hello wor"}

-- disconnect --
TCP RST from client

-- reconnect --
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Last-Event-ID: evt-18723

-- server sends --
: event: message
: id: evt-18723
: data: {"delta":"Hello wor"}
: event: message
: id: evt-18724
: data: {"delta":"ld\n"}
-- then we see a second sequence of evt-18723 again --
```

samir (eng-sre): hmm that suggests our resume path is re-emitting the acknowledged event but also reissuing generation that produced the same deltas. We need to correlate the `event.id` to token consumption and ensure billing increments only when new tokens are output.

jordan (Support Lead): customer is pushing for immediate refund. Support has already flagged billing ops. Can eng confirm probable root cause and a short ETA to mitigation?

samir (eng-sre): ETA: hotfix to resume handler to suppress duplicate emission + dedupe billing entries -> ~48 hours if we cut a targeted release. Longer if this requires changes to the billing pipeline. Meanwhile we can issue manual refunds for clearly-duplicated request_ids.

mike (Android Eng): changed SDK plan: v0.9.3 will add de-dupe by event id and expose `sseResumeConservative` toggle for customers that prefer safe resumes. Will try to ship within 24 hours as an emergency patch.

anna (Product): assign a small cross-functional incident: eng-sre (samir), android (mike), billing ops, support (ashley/jordan). We'll prepare customer comms: acknowledge bug, refund pending, ETA for fix.

dev-bot: incident created: INC-2026-4217 assigned -> samir, mike, jordan, billing-ops. Severity: p2 (customer impact).

ashley (Support): customer is fine with refund + SDK patch plan. They asked if we can provide a short-term proxy rule: "if resume request includes Last-Event-ID and the server's resume_point == lastEventId, return 204 No-Content and no billing" — would that be feasible quickly?

samir (eng-sre): yes we can add a short circuit in the ingress resume handler to return 204 when resume_point matches and no new tokens would be generated. That is lower-risk and could be rolled in hours. We'll coordinate with billing to ensure no meter entry is emitted for that path.

mike (Android Eng): will also add client-side conservative toggle and publish a patch. I'll attach a sample snippet for SDK consumers to turn it on now:
```kotlin
val client = RedwoodSSEClient.Builder()
  .setUrl("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream")
  .setSseResumeConservative(true) // ignore server-duplicated events when resume happens
  .build()
```
ashley (Support): thanks team. I'll tell the customer: refund in progress, short-term server-side 204 rule being deployed, and SDK patch expected in 24h. Keeping this thread open for updates. :thumbsup:

samir (eng-sre): will post deploy timeline in ~30m.

mike (Android Eng): starting SDK patch now.

anna (Product): good. afterwards let's add an automated test that simulates client RST + resume to ensure we don't regress.

ashley (Support): noted, will follow up with billing ticket number and customer email.

dev-bot: INC-2026-4217 updated: resume-shortcircuit patch merged to canary.

samir (eng-sre): canary looks good. will schedule rollout to production in 2h unless any objections.

jordan (Support Lead): roll forward. keep customer update pinned.

ashley (Support): closing loop with customer now, will post refund id and patch notes after prod rollout.
